Distribution and quantile functions of the wrapped skew generalised normal distribution

Source: R/wsgnstat.R
pwsgn.Rd

The distribution function is measured anticlockwise from angle 0: pwsgn(theta) is the probability of the arc [0, theta], computed as the sum over turns of the line law's mass on [2 pi k, theta + 2 pi k] through the regularised incomplete gamma function, so no numerical quadrature is involved. The quantile function inverts it by bisection. The identified parameterisation of dwsgn is used.

Usage

pwsgn(q, mu = 0, beta = 2, lam = 0.5, K = 50)

qwsgn(p, mu = 0, beta = 2, lam = 0.5, K = 50)

Arguments

q

numeric vector of angles in radians.

mu

location (junction) parameter; for a skew law this is not the mean direction.

beta

shape (tail) parameter (> 0).

lam

skewness parameter in (0, 1); 0.5 is symmetric.

K

truncation of the wrapping sum (abs(k) <= K). The default 50 captures the whole mass to double precision for beta >= 0.8; for very heavy tails (beta near 0.3) it does not, and pwsgn(2 * pi, mu, beta, lam, K) reports the mass that the truncated sum captures, so K can be raised until that is one.

p

numeric vector of probabilities.

Value

pwsgn gives probabilities in [0, 1]: 0 for q <= 0 and, for q >= 2 * pi, the mass captured by the wrapping sum truncated at K (one to double precision unless the tails are very heavy; see dwsgn). qwsgn gives angles in [0, 2 * pi], with a warning for any p above the captured mass.

Examples

## the distribution function is the integral of the density
pwsgn(2, mu = 1, beta = 1.5, lam = 0.3)
#> [1] 0.6921913
integrate(dwsgn, 0, 2, mu = 1, beta = 1.5, lam = 0.3)$value
#> [1] 0.6921913
## the quantile function inverts it
p <- c(0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.95)
q <- qwsgn(p, mu = 1, beta = 1.5, lam = 0.3)
rbind(p, pwsgn(q, mu = 1, beta = 1.5, lam = 0.3))
#>   [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] [,5]
#> p 0.05 0.25  0.5 0.75 0.95
#>   0.05 0.25  0.5 0.75 0.95
## the curve rises from 0 to 1 around the circle
th <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 361)
plot(th, pwsgn(th, mu = 1, beta = 1.5, lam = 0.3), type = "l",
     xlab = "angle (radians)", ylab = "distribution function")
